Location: Crawley, United Kingdom
Thales is a global technology leader with more than 83,000 employees on five continents. With over 7,500 people in the UK, operating across defence, space, aerospace, and digital security, we help build a future we can all trust. Thales supports the security and stability of our nation by providing extraordinary technology to our customers, as well as delivering social value to the UK with our products and services.
Join a proven firmware engineering team delivering advanced solutions for defence and related electronic systems. You will help design, develop and verify FPGA firmware for mission-critical products, working with modern FPGA and System-on-Chip technologies in a structured, quality-driven engineering environment.
This is an opportunity to shape reusable firmware architectures, solve complex technical challenges, and influence how firmware is designed, verified and delivered across multi-disciplinary programmes.
What you’ll do
• Architect FPGA firmware designs that promote reuse, scalability and maintainability.
• Design FPGA firmware using VHDL or SystemVerilog.
• Verify FPGA firmware using Hardware Verification Languages or Hardware Description Languages.
• Develop and improve verification test benches, simulation environments and verification methodologies.
• Work alongside systems, software and hardware engineers to deliver complete electronic systems.
• Contribute to requirements definition, architecture, design, verification and validation.
• Enhance firmware processes through documentation, scripting, reporting and automation.
• Collaborate effectively with internal teams, customers and integration facilities.
• Deliver firmware projects to agreed time, cost and quality targets.
What we’re looking for
You will bring demonstrable firmware engineering experience within defence, aerospace or transportation, ideally including exposure to external customers and internal engineering stakeholders.
Essential experience
• A relevant degree in Electronics or a related discipline — BEng, MEng, EngD or PhD.
• You will bring demonstrable experience in FPGA firmware design and verification, including the ability to deliver complex firmware solutions within a structured engineering environment.
• Strong FPGA design experience using VHDL or SystemVerilog.
• Experience verifying FPGA firmware using test benches and simulation tools.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to work independently while contributing within a multi-disciplinary team.
Desirable technical experience
• FPGA architectures: Xilinx/AMD, Altera/Intel, Microsemi/Microchip, Lattice.
• Development tools: Vivado, Vitis, Quartus, Libero, Diamond, Radiant, Precision or Propel.
• Verification methodologies: OSVVM, UVVM or UVM.
• Simulation tools: Siemens ModelSim/QuestaSim or AMD XSim.
• Scripting: TCL and/or Python.
• Requirements management: IBM Rational DOORS or Siemens Polarion.
• Interface and protocol knowledge: PCIe, Ethernet, serial communications, AXI4, OCP, Wishbone, JESD204, CameraLink or SMPTE.
• Object-oriented design techniques.
• Algorithm development using MATLAB or Simulink.
• Linux development environments.
• Familiarity with process assurance standards such as DO-254, IEC 61508, ISO 26262 or OpenCPI.
• Awareness of cyber-security standards, particularly IEC 62443.
What we offer
As a People 1st Employer, we are committed to supporting your long-term engineering career. You will have access to:
• Support for Professional Registration applications, including Chartership.
• Funding for membership of a relevant professional engineering body.
• A comprehensive e-learning platform and structured development pathways.
• Clear progression routes towards Firmware Architect, Firmware Engineering Manager, or recognised Thales Specialist or Expert roles.
• Hybrid working, with regular time required at customer sites and/or integration facilities.
Who will thrive here
You will be a proactive team player with a “can-do” attitude, comfortable solving complex problems and asking challenging questions. You will manage your own workload effectively, contribute to wider operational goals, and bring ideas that strengthen our products, processes and engineering capability.
We welcome candidates who promote inclusiveness, collaboration and diverse thinking in everything they do.
Security Clearance Requirement:
Due to the nature of the work that we do at Thales, many of our roles are subject to security restrictions.  This role requires Security Clearance (SC). It would be advantageous if currently held, however, if not currently held, it is a requirement that the successful applicant undergo, achieve, and maintain SC Clearance prior to commencing employment.
To be eligible for full SC, you generally need to have resided in the UK for the last 5 years.  In some circumstances, a minimum of 3 years’ residence in the UK over the last 5 years may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.
Please visit the UKSV website for further guidance:

Our Engineering internship is structured differently to all other internships and is designed to give you a real appreciation of what it means to work for us as an Engineer. The programme emphasises agile ways of working and immerses you in a dynamic and collaborative environment in which you’ll get to work in Scrums on real business projects supported by engineering experts.

• Learning about how we operate, and how the contribution of Engineering makes a difference across our business technology functions including Retail, Wealth, Commercial & Institutional and Customer & Operations
• Learning how engineers collaborate with AI tools and emerging agentic technologies to solve complex problems while applying human judgement and critical thinking
• Building an understanding of the products and services we provide for our customers and colleagues
• Attending Engineering specific networking events, social engagements and the opportunity to hear from senior leaders across the bank
How you’ll benefit
We’ll reward you with a starting salary of £29,400 pro rata.
Plus, you can expect to:
• Learn from industry experts and immediately apply your learnings
• Enrich your learning with access to our Learning Academy
• Test and learn new approaches in a safe, inclusive environment
• Start building a professional network
• Grow your confidence, build your resilience, and elevate your presence
• Experience first-hand what it’s like working in a purpose-driven organisation
Entry requirements

• To be in your penultimate year of university

Job Title
MarTech Lead (Data & AI)
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in
established businesses.
The bar is high - bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your team
Our MarTech team is evolving as we take on projects that will reshape how we communicate with clients, personalise their experiences, improve marketing performance and embed AI into how our marketing teams work. As MarTech Lead, you will drive the successful delivery of a complex and evolving marketing technology roadmap spanning customer engagement, data infrastructure, performance marketing measurement and AI enablement.
Your role in the Team’s Success
We're looking for a hands-on MarTech Lead to take technical ownership of our marketing technology stack, not just manage the roadmap, but get into the data and fix what's broken. You'll lead two flagship projects: building a single source of truth by integrating and reconciling data across 40+ tools (Braze, GA4/BigQuery, Salesforce, and more) and owning our SFMC (Salesforce Marketing Cloud) to Braze migration end-to-end, including data validation and technical sign-off. Day to day, you'll diagnose data quality issues directly and use AI tooling to automate the manual work that used to take a whole team. This is a technical role at heart, strong data engineering fundamentals and real fluency with AI-assisted workflows matter more here than project management polish.
What you’ll do
Own the SFMC -> Braze Migration
• Act as the technical owner of the SFMC → Braze migration: own the plan, sequencing, and cutover strategy, not just a workstream within it
• Personally validate data and journey parity between SFMC and Braze, reconciling records, logic, and event data at the SQL/pipeline level, not just sign-off via a status report
• Identify and fix migration-related data issues directly (mapping errors, duplicate/missing events, broken triggers) rather than logging tickets for someone else to resolve
• Own the technical relationship with Client Tech and Data Architecture for everything migration-related, uptime, data integrity, and rollback/contingency planning
Build the source of truth data
• Define the technical architecture for a unique source of truth, schema design, identity resolution/stitching across tools, update cadence, and ownership of conflicts when tools disagree
• Manage integrations of 3rd-party tools, understanding the technical data contracts involved, spec how data from disparate tools should be integrated, deduplicated, and reconciled into a single, trusted data store.
• Work with Data Architecture and the data warehouse team to align this with the existing BigQuery/attribution setup
• Build validation/monitoring so the source of truth is trusted by default, flag drift or breakage before stakeholders notice bad numbers
Technical Ownership
• Diagnose and resolve data quality issues directly. Duplicate events, integer overflow/ID issues, broken field mappings, integration failures rather than escalating to a data engineer
• Write and maintain SQL/Python for data validation, QA scripts, and user journey debugging.
• Use AI tools (LLM-based agents, scripting, internal automation) to speed up recurring MarTech work: QA checks, documentation, campaign audits, migration validation, training material generation etc.
• Manage vendor relationships
What you’ll need for this role
You're a technologist first, not a project coordinator. Someone who's more comfortable in a SQL console or a data pipeline than in a status meeting, and who reaches for AI tools instinctively to move faster rather than waiting for someone else to build the tool for you.
You are comfortable operating in ambiguity, able to connect the dots between teams and skilled at turning broad goals into practical technical plans. You understand how marketing technology, measurement and data work together at a hands-on level, not just conceptually.
You will likely bring:
• Strong ability to translate business objectives into structured delivery plans, requirements and documentation.
• Clear, confident communication skills with the ability to work effectively across teams with different priorities, disciplines and levels of technical understanding.
• Experience managing multiple initiatives in parallel, including coordination of external vendors and delivery partners, while maintaining focus on outcomes.
• Strong SQL and comfort working in BigQuery or an equivalent warehouse. You can write your own validation queries, not just request them
• Working proficiency in Python (or another mainstream language) for scripting data checks, automation, and pipeline debugging
• Practical experience building with AI/LLM tools. Automating a workflow, building an internal agent, or similar beyond casual chatbot use
• Experience owning (not just contributing to) at least one platform migration or major data integration project
• Comfort designing data architecture, schema decisions, identity resolution, reconciling conflicting data across systems
The Perks
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.
• Competitive salary
• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
• The option to buy or sell holiday days
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
• Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay and leave, as well as a range of support and benefits for parents

Reusable "starter kits" aligned to the AI-First Strategy build plan (e.g., Maintenance automation kit, AI-SDLC kit, Commercial/Sales acceleration kit).

Reference architectures and implementation patterns that work across heterogeneous BU stacks (Azure, AWS, on-prem, legacy products).

hyperiongrp.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/broadb.description_excerpt:
Who are we?
Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.
People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.
Role Purpose
The Strategic Data & Analytics team builds the analytical products that support growth across Howden Employee Benefits. We are a business-embedded team that works directly alongside consultants, client directors and project teams, rather than operating within a traditional technology or IT function. Our products are used every day by colleagues across the UK business and by our clients to support better decision-making, solve complex challenges and deliver stronger outcomes.
This role builds those products. You will own delivery end to end, and lead the reusable components, frameworks, templates and working practices that allow a small team to serve the whole business. Our approach is simple: build fewer things, build them fast, and build them once so they can be used many times.
This is not a software engineering role and it is not an IT role. We are a consulting team that is proficient with technology. You will spend as much time working out what a senior leader actually needs to decide as writing the code that answers it.
Location is flexible, with home-based or local Howden office-based both available according to preference. The team itself is distributed across home and several Howden offices and works together primarily over Teams rather than in one room. Our closeness to the business is organisational rather than geographic.
Key Accountabilities
• Work directly with senior leaders and client-facing colleagues to turn a broad commercial question into a defined, decidable one, and to turn the answer into a product rather than a one-off analysis.
• Own delivery of analytical products end to end, from first conversations through to something in production that real users depend on.
• Lead the development of the reusable components, libraries, frameworks, templates and working practices the rest of the team builds on.
• Build for reuse and hand-off: configurable, documented and maintainable by someone other than you.
• Work within the firm’s software development lifecycle and governance requirements, and help shape them where they do not yet fit how a small product team works.
• Support the technical development of colleagues, including reviewing their work. This is not a line management role.
• Keep delivery momentum when priorities move, which they will.
Skills & Experience
The first question is whether this is the right environment for you.
• You have a consulting mindset and enjoy working across a wide variety of problems.
• You enjoy helping senior leaders and their teams make better decisions, and you see data, analytics and visualisation as your tools for bringing that about.
• You can explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• You support the people around you, in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges. You share what you learn, you would rather have an honest conversation than a comfortableone, and you build your own network across the business. In a small team we succeed together, and nothing we build succeeds unless the business succeeds with it.
• You take ownership of your decisions, your actions and your outputs.
• You are comfortable with uncertainty and speed, and are interested rather than frustrated by new problems with incomplete and ambiguous information.
• You can work in a fast-growing firm where processes, systems and structures are still being brought together, and where parts of the environment are incomplete.
• You are effective in a distributed team. Most of our collaboration, with each other and with the business, happens over Teams, with colleagues you will meet in person occasionally rather than daily. If you do your best work by turning to the person beside you, this will be a difficult environment.
Technical experience:
• You have taken more than one analytical product from an incomplete brief through to sustained use by people who did not commission it. Delivery matters to us more than cleverness.
• You have built the reusable parts that colleagues then worked from, and you have lived with what you built after release: supported it, changed it under pressure, and let that change how you build next time. This would not be your first role building analytical products.
• You have substantial experience building analytical products in Python. Our stack is Python, Shiny for Python, Quarto, git, Azure DevOps for repositories, pipelines and artifacts, with Docker-based deployment and Terraform. We expect real experience of many of these, or of close equivalents such as R and Shiny, the tidyverse, Streamlit, Dash, or scientific and quantitative computing. We do not expect all of them.
You must be able to build without AI coding agents. We do not use them for coding. You will read, write, debug and review code yourself, and be able to explain all of it. If any material part of how you work today depends on agent-assisted or “vibe” coding, this is not the role for you, and we would rather you knew that before applying.
Experience of Employee Benefits, Pensions or Insurance is not required.
What do we offer in return?
A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
•
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
•
We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
•
We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond
Reasonable adjustments
We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs.  Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.
If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.
*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.
Permanent

Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) – England & Wales
Reporting To: SHEQ Manager
Location: England & Wales – project based with regular travel to live construction sites
Function: SHEQ / Environment
Role Purpose
The Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) will provide specialist ecological advice, assurance and site-based support across infrastructure and construction projects throughout England and Wales.
Reporting to the SHEQ Manager, the role will ensure that construction activities are planned and undertaken in accordance with ecological legislation, planning conditions, client requirements, environmental permits, licences and project environmental commitments.
The role will work closely with project management, engineering, construction and environmental teams to identify ecological risks at an early stage and ensure appropriate mitigation is incorporated into the planning and delivery of works.
A key element of the position will be providing practical ECoW support on live construction sites, including pre-construction surveys, ecological inspections, watching briefs, toolbox talks and monitoring of sensitive works.
Key Responsibilities
Ecological Clerk of Works
• Act as ECoW for construction activities where ecological supervision or specialist advice is required.
• Undertake pre-construction ecological checks and surveys.
• Provide ecological watching briefs during potentially sensitive construction activities.
• Identify ecological constraints and communicate appropriate controls to project teams.
• Stop, pause or escalate works where there is a risk of ecological harm or breach of licence, consent or legal requirement.
• Provide advice on appropriate exclusion zones, buffers and working methods.
• Maintain accurate records of ecological inspections, observations, interventions and actions.
Protected Species
Provide specialist advice and site support relating to protected and notable species including, where relevant:
• Bats.
• Badgers.
• Great crested newts.
• Otters.
• Water voles.
• Reptiles.
• Breeding and nesting birds.
• Barn owls.
• Dormice.
• Invasive non-native species.
• Other protected or priority species identified through project surveys.
Ensure project teams understand and comply with applicable protected species licences and mitigation requirements.
Surveys & Assessments
• Undertake or coordinate Preliminary Ecological Appraisals (PEAs).
• Support UKHab habitat surveys and condition assessments.
• Undertake protected species surveys within the individual's competence and relevant professional guidance.
• Review ecological survey reports produced by consultants.
• Support ecological input into Environmental Impact Assessments and project environmental documentation.
• Identify requirements for additional specialist surveys and consultants.
Construction Support
• Review RAMS and construction methodologies from an ecological perspective.
• Provide ecological input into Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMPs).
• Support preparation and implementation of Ecological Management Plans and Species Protection Plans.
• Undertake pre-start briefings and ecological toolbox talks.
• Work collaboratively with Site Managers, Engineers and Supervisors to develop practical solutions to ecological constraints.
• Attend construction and environmental planning meetings where required.
Biodiversity Net Gain
• Support project compliance with applicable Biodiversity Net Gain requirements.
• Assist with baseline habitat assessments and condition assessments.
• Support development and implementation of biodiversity enhancement measures.
• Monitor delivery of habitat creation, restoration and enhancement commitments.
• Support collection and maintenance of evidence required to demonstrate delivery of biodiversity commitments.
Environmental Compliance
Provide ecological advice in relation to applicable requirements including:
• Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
• Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017.
• Protection of Badgers Act 1992.
• Environment Act 2021.
• Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
• Natural Environment and Rural Communities Act 2006.
• Applicable planning conditions, licences and consents.
Maintain awareness of legislative and regulatory changes relevant to project activities.
Pollution Prevention & Environmental Support
While primarily an ecological role, provide environmental support where required, particularly where construction activities could affect:
• Watercourses and aquatic habitats.
• Protected sites.
• Trees and vegetation.
• Sensitive habitats.
• Soil and habitat reinstatement.
• Invasive species.
• Habitat fragmentation and disturbance.
Ecological Incidents
• Respond to ecological incidents, unexpected discoveries and potential breaches.
• Provide immediate advice to project teams on appropriate actions.
• Support environmental incident investigations.
• Liaise with the SHEQ Manager and Environmental Manager regarding significant ecological issues.
• Support regulatory notifications where required.
• Ensure lessons learned are communicated across project teams.
Stakeholder Engagement
Develop effective relationships with project teams, clients, landowners, environmental consultants and statutory bodies including Natural England, Natural Resources Wales and relevant local authorities.
Represent the project at ecological and environmental meetings where required.
Reporting & Assurance
• Produce ecological inspection and monitoring reports.
• Maintain ecological constraints and action registers.
• Track ecological actions through to closure.
• Provide ecological information for project SHEQ reporting.
• Support client environmental audits and assurance visits.
• Maintain appropriate evidence demonstrating compliance with licences, planning conditions and ecological commitments.
Key Accountabilities
The role is accountable for:
• Effective identification and management of ecological risks.
• Delivery of competent ECoW support.
• Compliance with protected species requirements.
• Implementation of ecological mitigation measures.
• Accurate ecological records and evidence.
• Timely escalation of significant ecological risks.
• Supporting delivery of project biodiversity commitments.
• Preventing avoidable ecological harm arising from construction activities.
Essential Qualifications
• Degree or equivalent qualification in Ecology, Environmental Science, Conservation Biology or a related discipline.
• Appropriate professional membership of CIEEM or equivalent.
• Good working knowledge of ecological legislation applicable to England and Wales.
• Full UK Driving Licence.
Desirable Qualifications
• Associate or Full Membership of CIEEM.
• Protected species survey licences relevant to the project portfolio.
• CSCS/ECS or equivalent construction site competence.
• ECoW training or demonstrable equivalent experience.
• UKHab training.
• Biodiversity Net Gain assessment experience.
• Environmental auditing…

As a Satellites AIT Craft Apprentice, you'll be part of a team and gain hands-on experience in a supportive and innovative environment, contributing to projects that push the boundaries of technology.
This programme is perfect for those with a passion for both mechanical and electrical precision, a knack for problem-solving, and a keen interest in seeing their work take flight. Join us in shaping the future of space exploration!
What you will be doing
Year 1: You will study towards a Level 2 Engineering Operative ST0537 on the electrical pathway, gaining both academic knowledge and practical experience.
Year 2: During the Apprenticeship you will have a unique opportunity to experience our Satellites AIT Production area of the business which will provide you with a comprehensive understanding of how a Satellite is manufactured at Airbus Defence & Space.
This includes working in small teams or on a one-to-one basis to manufacture Satellites using the latest approved processes and advanced production techniques for Satellite manufacture.
Your key activities & responsibilities will be:
Mechanical Assembly
• Use of various different adhesives and bonding methods
• Use of hand measuring tools to meet tight tolerances
• Installation of various components to satellite structures
• Installation of various connector brackets
• Bonding of Heater Mats, Thermocouples and Thermostats to various surfaces
• Following process and tolerances to drawings on 3DX
Electrical
• Perform electrical assembly, integration and modification of electrical systems (harness routing, electrical connection, soldering, crimping).
• Perform basic electrical tests (continuity, bonding, insulation, DC high voltage).
• Perform first level quality inspection.
• You will handle raw materials, tools, standard parts and components, documentation (technical instruction, work order, test procedure, job card, etc).
Year 3: You will be fully on-site, fine tuning your hand skills against the business skills matrix.
Requirements
• Funding Eligibility: Applicants must be aged 16–21* and cannot hold a Level 2 or higher qualification (e.g., NVQ, BTEC, HND, or Degree) in Engineering, Aerospace, or related technical fields. For more information, please consult Foundation Apprenticeships Criteria*
• Education: No strict formal entry requirements, though a Grade 3 (or equivalent) in GCSE Maths and English is desirable.
• Skills & Attributes: Strong communication, reliability, excellent work ethic, a can-do attitude, and the ability to follow technical instructions and work well independently or in a team.
• No prior experience required—full on-the-job training will be provided.
BOOST YOUR APPLICATION

What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? Is it our aircraft, innovation, global impact, or something else? Let us know what interests you about our work and why we stand out to you.

To design, develop and improve software, utilising various engineering methodologies, that provides business, platform, and technology capabilities for our customers and colleagues.
Accountabilities
• Development and delivery of high-quality software solutions by using industry aligned programming languages, frameworks, and tools. Ensuring that code is scalable, maintainable, and optimized for performance.

• Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategies.

As a Software Engineer within Barclaycard Payments, you will help design, build and operate customer-facing products that support one of the UK's leading payments businesses. Working across the technology stack, you will contribute to the delivery of scalable solutions, collaborate with experienced engineering teams and play a key role in shaping the future of a business undergoing significant transformation.
Barclaycard Payments processes billions of pounds of payments annually for businesses across the UK. Through our strategic partnership with Brookfield Asset Management, we are transforming the business into a standalone fintech focused on innovation, growth and customer outcomes.

You'll collaborate with engineers, product teams and business stakeholders to develop high-quality solutions, contribute to technical improvements and support the ongoing evolution of our technology landscape.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

• Experience within payments, fintech or technology-led organisations.
• Knowledge of AI technologies and machine learning integration.
• Experience with technologies such as Rust, Kotlin, TypeScript or React.
• Knowledge of Kubernetes, cloud-native platforms and containerisation technologies.
• Experience with DevOps practices, CI/CD methodologies and infrastructure as code.
• Knowledge of event-driven architecture, messaging technologies and API development.
This role is based in London. We support a hybrid working model, with colleagues expected to attend the office three days per week. Participation in an on-call rota may also be required.
You may be assessed on the key critical skills relevant for success in role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen, strategic thinking and digital and technology, as well as job-specific technical skills.

•
Ensure the efficient running of the shop floor, in order to achieve the highest levels of customer service, sales and profit.
•
Support the Management team managing all personnel, product and merchandising functions, business processes and results for their store.
•
Communicate with staff daily their individual sales goals, key performance indicators, store results, product sales and other information to help them provide unparalleled service and achieve.
•
Hold ‘one minute meetings’ at the end of employees’ shifts; summarise their performance results, provide constructive feedback and recognition.
•
Execute and model company established best practices in Customer Service, Store Operations, Loss Prevention,and Point of Sale.
•
Achieve company standards/goals for personal sales results: sales v. budgets, sales per hour and units per transaction.
•
Respond to and communicate with the Store Manager on all competitors, community information that could impact company business.
•
Focus staff on the importance of quality relationships with internal and external customers.
•
Effectively manage customer complaints in a timely and effective way.
•
Analyse store level reports and create action plans to improve results.
•
Effectively communicate with the Store Manager regarding day-to-day operational issues of the store.
•
Perform Manager-on-duty functions; manage store opening/closing functions and the sales floor.
About YOU
•
You'll have a previous track record of supervisory or specialist roles within a premium or luxury brand.
•
You'll have previous people management experience with the ability to resolve conflict and unproductive disagreements.
•
You'll be an effective communicator with the ability to build relationships with ease.
•
You'll be a team player who recognises and celebrates the contributions and achievements of others.
•
You'll be confident in giving feedback that promotes positive behavioral change.
•
You will work well with change, being able to quickly adapt and work with pace.
•
You will be energetic and authentic showing a clear presence on the shop floor.
•
You'll approach all issues with a ‘can do’ approach and act with initiative to find in store solutions.

At PVH, we understand that the success of our organisation is directly related to our hardworking and dedicated associates who contribute their time and talents to help make our Company the success it is. Title:
Tax Manager
KBR is a global provider of differentiated, professional services and technologies delivered across a wide government, defense and industrial base. KBR is proud to work with its customers across the globe to provide technology, value-added services, and long-term operations and maintenance services to ensure consistent delivery with predictable results.
At KBR, We Deliver.
Tax Manager - UK, Europe & Africa
Location: Leatherhead / Hybrid working arrangement
The Role
Reporting to the Regional Head of Tax, the Tax Manager will play an important role in managing tax risks, supporting the business and ensuring compliance across the region.
The successful candidate will have strong VAT expertise but will also work across a broad range of tax matters, including corporate tax, withholding tax and business projects. The role offers an opportunity to develop into a well-rounded regional tax professional while working closely with stakeholders across Finance, Legal, Operations and the wider Tax function.
The role will also support KBR's tax transformation programme, including process improvements, systems initiatives and the continued development of the regional tax function.
What You'll Be Doing
Indirect Tax
• Manage KBR's VAT compliance obligations across the UK, Europe and Africa, ensuring timely and accurate filing across all VAT registrations in the region.
• Review VAT returns and other indirect tax filings, working with external advisers and local Finance teams where required.
• Support VAT audits and enquiries from tax authorities.
• Provide VAT advisory support to business and project teams.
• Manage VAT registrations, deregistrations and indirect tax reporting requirements across the region.
• Support VAT-related systems, controls and process improvements.
Corporate Tax & Tax Advisory
• Support corporate tax compliance activities across the region.
• Review customer and supplier contracts from a tax perspective.
• Support legal entity restructurings, acquisitions, integrations and other business initiatives.
• Support tax audits, enquiries and disputes across multiple jurisdictions.
• Assist with tax planning, risk management and advisory projects.
Tax Governance & Risk
• Support SOX and Senior Accounting Officer (SAO) controls across the region.
• Maintain tax process documentation and support continuous improvement initiatives.
• Assist with the preparation of tax risk assessments and governance reporting.
• Support the development and implementation of tax policies and procedures.
• Help ensure compliance with internal controls and group tax policies.
Tax Transformation & Projects
• Support tax technology, ERP and e-invoicing projects across the region.
• Contribute to process improvement and automation initiatives.
• Work with Finance, IT and external providers to improve the quality and efficiency of tax processes.
• Support wider regional and global tax projects as required.
Training & Knowledge Sharing
• Provide practical tax guidance to Finance and operational teams.
• Support the development of tax awareness across the business.
• Contribute to internal training materials and guidance notes.
• Assist in developing tax capability within the wider regional tax team.
What You'll Bring
• CTA, ACA, ACCA or equivalent professional qualification.
• Strong practical experience in VAT and indirect taxes within a multinational environment.
• Experience managing relationships with external advisers and tax authorities.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities across a wide geographical region.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• A proactive and collaborative approach
KBR Company Information
When you become part of the KBR team, your opportunities are endless. Through collaboration with our customers, we’re defining tomorrow’s challenges, then providing the solutions and services to overcome those challenges, always maintaining our commitment to total safety and reliability.
At KBR, we partner with government and industry clients to provide purposeful and comprehensive solutions with an emphasis on efficiency and safety. With a full portfolio of services, proprietary technologies and expertise, our employees are ready to handle projects and missions throughout their entire lifecycle, from planning and design to sustainability and maintenance. Whether at the bottom of the ocean or in outer space, our clients trust us to deliver the impossible on a daily basis.
Working at KBR means being rewarded for your contributions. In addition to competitive benefits and professional development, our people are empowered to use all their potential, creating meaningful change for themselves and our clients. We attract the best minds in the world because our expertise thrives on creativity, resourcefulness and collaboration. That is how we supply our clients with cutting-edge solutions and services.
As the needs of the world change, we’re ready to respond and guide the way forward with strategic, sustainable, and technological advancements grounded in more than a century of practical application and execution.
